questions.stem: White light is made up of:

options.text: A mixture of all colours (wavelengths) of visible light
Only red, green, and blue light

questions.explanation: White light is a mixture of all colours (wavelengths) of visible light. It can be split into a spectrum using a prism.

questions.stem: What are the three primary colours of light?
questions.explanation: The three primary colours of light are red, green, and blue. These cannot be made by mixing other colours of light.

questions.stem: When red light and green light are mixed together, the result is:
questions.explanation: Red + green = yellow in additive colour mixing (light). This is different from mixing paints, which uses subtractive mixing.

options.text: Transmitting red light and absorbing all other colours
Adding red light to the beam
Converting all light into red light

questions.explanation: A colour filter works by transmitting (allowing through) its own colour and absorbing all other colours. A red filter transmits red and absorbs green, blue, etc.

questions.stem: A red object appears red because it:

options.text: Transmits red light through its surface
Absorbs red light and reflects all other colours
Reflects red light and absorbs other colours

questions.explanation: A red object reflects red wavelengths and absorbs other colours. The reflected red light reaches our eyes, making the object appear red.

questions.stem: What colour would a blue object appear under pure red light?
questions.explanation: A blue object reflects only blue light. Under pure red light, there is no blue light to reflect, so the object absorbs all the red light and appears black.

questions.stem: The splitting of white light into a spectrum by a prism is called:
questions.explanation: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its component colours. It occurs because different wavelengths of light refract by different amounts in the prism.
